arxiv-2104-03567.title: On the resolution of a weak Fermi paradox
arxiv-2104-03567.creator: Osmanov Z.N
arxiv-2104-03567.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Osmanov Z.N. In this paper we consider the Fermi’s paradox (FP) and propose a possible resolution in the context of super-advanced alien civilizations. In this sense it can be regarded as to be the weak Fermi paradox (WFP). By assuming that superadvanced extraterrestrials (ET) exist and are capable of constructing a huge ring-like megastructure around a pulsar or a main sequence star (MSS) to consume its emitted energy, we consider the stability problem of the ring, studying the out of plane dynamics.

arxiv-2305-14252.title: Quantum Kolmogorov complexity and quantum correlations in deterministic-control quantum Turing machines
arxiv-2305-14252.creator: Mariano Lemus, Ricardo Faleiro, Paulo Mateus, Nikola Paunković, André Souto
arxiv-2305-14252.description: Abstract This work presents a study of Kolmogorov complexity for general quantum states from the perspective of deterministic-control quantum Turing Machines (dcq-TM). We extend the dcq-TM model to incorporate mixed state inputs and outputs, and define dcq-computable states as those that can be approximated by a dcq-TM.

arxiv-2310-10575.title: Matching the Neuronal Representations of V1 is Necessary to Improve Robustness in CNNs with V1-like Front-ends
arxiv-2310-10575.creator: Ruxandra Barbulescu ∗,1, Tiago Marques ∗,2, Arlindo L. Oliveira 1,3 ∗ Joint first authors (equal contribution) 1 INESC-ID Lisboa, Portugal 2 Breast Unit, Champalimaud Clinical Center, Champalimaud Foundation, Lisboa, Portugal 3 IST Técnico Lisboa, Universidade de Lisboa, Portugal ruxi@inesc-id.pt ti
arxiv-2310-10575.description: Abstract While some convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved great success in object recognition, they struggle to identify objects in images corrupted with different types of common noise patterns. Recently, it was shown that simulating computations in early visual areas at the front of CNNs leads to improvements in robustness to image corruptions.

arxiv-2405-04416.title: DistGrid: Scalable Scene Reconstruction with Distributed Multi-resolution Hash Grid 344 Journal: TOG CCS: Computing methodologies Reconstruction CCS: Computing methodologies Rendering CCS: Computer systems organization Neural networks
arxiv-2405-04416.creator: Sidun Liu, Peng Qiao, Zongxin Ye, Wenyu Li, Yong Dou
arxiv-2405-04416.description: Abstract . Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) achieves extremely high quality in object-scaled and indoor scene reconstruction. However, there exist some challenges when reconstructing large-scale scenes. MLP-based NeRFs suffer from limited network capacity, while volume-based NeRFs are heavily memory-consuming when the scene resolution increases. Recent approaches propose to geographically partition the scene and learn each sub-region using an individual NeRF.

arxiv-2406-11264.title: Input-to-State Stabilization of 1 1 -D Parabolic PDEs under Output Feedback Control
arxiv-2406-11264.creator: Yongchun Bi 1, Jun Zheng 1,2, Guchuan Zhu 2
arxiv-2406-11264.description: Abstract This paper addresses the problem of input-to-state stabilization for a class of parabolic equations with time-varying coefficients, as well as Dirichlet and Robin boundary disturbances. By using time-invariant kernel functions, which can reduce the complexity in control design and implementation, an observer-based output feedback controller is designed via backstepping.

arxiv-2410-03176.title: Investigating and Mitigating Object Hallucinations in Pretrained Vision-Language (CLIP) Models
arxiv-2410-03176.creator: Yufang Liu, Tao Ji, Changzhi Sun, Yuanbin Wu, Aimin ZhouSchool of Computer Science and Technology, East China Normal University School of Computer Science, Fudan University Pazhou Laboratory, Huangpu
arxiv-2410-03176.description: Abstract Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved impressive performance, yet research has pointed out a serious issue with object hallucinations within these models. However, there is no clear conclusion as to which part of the model these hallucinations originate from.

arxiv-2506-09048.title: Understanding Task Vectors in In-Context Learning: Emergence, Functionality, and Limitations
arxiv-2506-09048.creator: Yuxin Dong, Jiachen Jiang, Zhihui Zhu, Xia Ning
arxiv-2506-09048.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuxin Dong, Jiachen Jiang, Zhihui Zhu, Xia Ning. Task vectors offer a compelling mechanism for accelerating inference in in-context learning (ICL) by distilling task-specific information into a single, reusable representation. Despite their empirical success, the underlying principles governing their emergence and functionality remain unclear. This work proposes the Linear Combination Conjecture , positing that task vectors act as single in-context demonstrations formed through linear combinations of the original ones. We provide both theoretical and empirical support for this conjecture.

pmc-10608037.title: Multifocal Tuberculosis Verrucosa Cutis: Case Report and Review of the Literature
pmc-10608037.creator: Niki Ntavari, Vasiliki Syrmou, Konstantinos Tourlakopoulos, Foteini Malli, Irini Gerogianni, Angeliki-Viktoria Roussaki, Efterpi Zafiriou, Maria Ioannou, Eirini Tziastoudi, Konstantinos I. Gourgoulianis, Ioannis Pantazopoulos
pmc-10608037.description: Cutaneous tuberculosis (TB) is still a major public health problem worldwide. Tuberculosis verrucosa cutis (TBVC) is a cutaneous form of exogenous TB caused by exogenous reinfection in previously sensitized individuals. TBVC typically presents as a unifocal condition. Multifocal cutaneous lesions without any other tubercular foci are extremely rare in exogenous TB and few cases are reported in the literature.

pmc-10609269.title: Heterogeneous Habitats in Taiga Forests with Different Important Values of Constructive Species Changes Bacterial Beta Diversity
pmc-10609269.creator: Tian Zhou, Song Wu, Hong Pan, Xinming Lu, Jun Du, Libin Yang, Acacio Aparecido Navarrete
pmc-10609269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). As a crucial link between the aboveground and belowground components of forest ecosystems, soil bacterial communities are extremely sensitive to changes in plant communities and soil conditions. To investigate the impact of the difference of constructive species on soil bacterial communities in taiga forests, we conducted a vegetation survey at the international monitoring plot of the Larix gmelinii forests in the Great Khingan Mountains and calculated the important value of Larix gmelinii to determine experimental groups based on this survey.

pmc-10755414.title: Prevalence of mental disorders in South Asia: A systematic review of reviews
pmc-10755414.creator: Aishwarya L. Vidyasagaran, David McDaid, Mehreen R. Faisal, Muhammad Nasir, Krishna P. Muliyala, Sreekanth Thekkumkara, Judy Wright, Rumana Huque, Saumit Benkalkar, Najma Siddiqi, Aishwarya Lakshmi Vidyasagaran, Aishwarya Lakshmi Vidyasagaran, Aishwarya Lakshmi Vidyasagaran
pmc-10755414.description: Mental disorders are increasing in South Asia (SA), but their epidemiological burden is under-researched. We carried out a systematic umbrella review to estimate the prevalence of mental disorders and intentional self-harm in the region. Multiple databases were searched and systematic reviews reporting the prevalence of at least one mental disorder from countries in SA were included.

pmc-11367551.title: TLR2/NF-кB signaling may control expansion and function of regulatory T cells in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS)
pmc-11367551.creator: Meng-Meng Li, Shan-Shan Hu, Ling Xu, Jing Gao, Xin Zheng, Xiu-Ling Li, Le-Le Liu
pmc-11367551.description: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a recently identified infectious ailment triggered by a new strain of bunyavirus. It is distinguished by elevated fatality rates, ranging from 12 % to 30 %. The mechanism underlying the development of severe illness caused by SFTS bunyavirus (SFTSV) is not yet fully understood.

pmc-12538103.title: Prospects of CCUS technology under resource utilization and environmental risks
pmc-12538103.creator: Lingna Liu, Chuanwang Liu, Jingxue Wei, Jianping Ge
pmc-12538103.description: SummaryCarbon dioxide capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a critical technology for global climate mitigation, supporting low-carbon fossil fuel use and decarbonization in hard-to-abate sectors. However, different CCUS technologies exhibit distinct trade-offs in terms of energy consumption, resource utilization, and environmental impacts.

pmc-12615727.title: Hemodynamic determinants of postoperative neurocognitive impairment using Random Forest analysis and partial dependence plots
pmc-12615727.creator: Faruk Sanberk Kiziltas, Ozhan Ozkan, Fatih Toptan, Ibrahim Kara, Zuhal Dogan, Kadir Gokmen, Esra Gundogdu Eryilmaz, Ali Fuat Erdem
pmc-12615727.description: This study investigated the effect of hemodynamic data during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) on neurocognitive impairment in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery using machine learning algorithms. Twenty-eight CABG patients were included in the study. Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, pulse (PLS), and SpO2 were recorded at 2.4-second intervals, yielding 730,870 data points (450,548 after artefact removal).

pmc-13266816.title: Intrapleural fibrinolytic therapy for pleural infection: a multicentre real-world comparison of dosing regimens
pmc-13266816.creator: Glenn Khai Wern Yong, Jonathan Jia Jun Wong, Xiaoe Zhang, Si Ling Young, Brian Lee Wei Chua, Qiao Li Tan, Imran Bin Mohamed Noor, Charlene Jin Yee Liew, Mindy Chu Ming Choong, Wui Mei Chew, Ken Junyang Goh
pmc-13266816.description: BackgroundAdvances in the non-surgical management of pleural infection using intrapleural alteplase and DNase have reshaped treatment strategies. While twice-daily intrapleural fibrinolytic therapy (IPFT) is commonly used, evidence supporting once-daily regimens remains limited. We aimed to describe real-world outcomes associated with once- and twice-daily IPFT regimens and to compare their efficacy and safety, including outcomes among patients receiving modified alteplase doses.
